ranked.headline: Omics inference methods are tested for replicability across cohorts and subgroups
ranked.summary: Multi-omics analyses increasingly require findings that replicate across cohorts and subgroups, not only within the discovery dataset.

ranked.headline: Graph, contrastive and transport models align single-cell and spatial omic modalities
ranked.summary: Items dated April to May 2026 extend learned cross-modal alignment from paired multi-omics to foundation models, spatial omics and histology.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence models drive protein, PROTAC, and molecule generation and prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add joint sequence-structure decoding and atomic diffusion alongside published PLM-based generation and prediction work.

ranked.headline: Learned models and statistical methods for single-cell and spatial omics analysis
ranked.summary: Multi-sample, spatial and multimodal single-cell datasets demand new preprocessing, testing and perturbation-prediction methods.

ranked.headline: Quantifying bias and reproducibility in statistical methods for omics data
ranked.summary: Recent work quantifies methodological bias, error control and replicability in omics statistics rather than reporting shared biological findings.

ranked.headline: Dynamical models of brain activity, amyloid spread and learned representations
ranked.summary: Recent preprints fit dynamical and data-driven models to amyloid PET, fMRI, neural recordings and low-rank RNNs to resolve temporal structure.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks test docking, rescoring and ML models for small-molecule binding prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers benchmark open-source docking and ML scoring against curated experimental affinity and activity data.

ranked.headline: Structure-informed tools map variants, modifications, and evolution onto 3D models
ranked.summary: Recent releases pair residue-level structural context with variant, modification, and evolutionary analysis at increasing scale.

ranked.headline: Genetic variants mapped to regulatory programs via chromatin, TF binding, and eQTLs
ranked.summary: Haplotype-resolved multiomics, deep learning, and multi-tissue eQTL models now resolve non-coding variant effects on regulation and disease.

ranked.headline: Adapting pretrained protein and language models to biological prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Recent work adapts protein language models and LLMs to function annotation, metadata curation and single-cell reasoning tasks.

ranked.headline: Hybrid and learned models capture stochastic and nonlinear biological dynamics
ranked.summary: Reduced, hybrid, and deep learning approaches now address stochastic and nonlinear dynamics across intracellular calcium signalling and bacterial growth.

ranked.headline: Scaffold splits expose limits of molecular model generalization under distribution shift
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and reliability frameworks test whether molecular and sequence models hold up when test data depart from training distributions.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings feed task-specific predictors of binding and function
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs ESM-2 and ProtT5 embeddings with interpretable architectures and tests whether embedding gains hold across tasks.

ranked.headline: Reviews trace shift from heuristics to deep learning in genomic prediction
ranked.summary: Benchmarks, curated datasets, and comparative resource audits now anchor evaluation of learned predictors across genomic and phase-separation tasks.

ranked.headline: Deep models infer gene regulatory networks and perturbation effects from single-cell data
ranked.summary: Transformers and causal architectures are now being built to infer regulatory structure and predict unseen perturbations from single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Graph neural networks predict chromatin loops, drug response, and molecular interactions
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 publications extend graph and multimodal learning across chromatin, drug, RNA, and protein prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks expose probe bias and platform differences in spatial transcriptomics
ranked.summary: Recent studies test spatial platforms against probe sequence alignments and computational inference, challenging the accuracy of targeted spatial panels.

ranked.headline: New phylogenetic software adds richer models, structure tests, and tree data reuse
ranked.summary: Recent open-source releases target gaps in model choice, population structure inference, and reuse of existing tree data.

ranked.headline: Learned representations drive RNA design, folding, and ensemble inference
ranked.summary: Generative and Bayesian models now target full-length mRNA design and family-robust RNA folding from chemical mapping data.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-level assemblies of red alga, wild rice, nematode and foxglove genomes
ranked.summary: Long-read and Hi-C scaffolding now yield gap-free and chromosome-scale references across diverse eukaryotes, from macroalgae to nematodes.

ranked.headline: Genetic and omic inputs inform predictive models of disease risk and biomarker discovery
ranked.summary: Multi-trait scores, multi-omics benchmarks and ancestry-aware GWAS tools show how added complexity and genetic structure affect prediction performance.

ranked.headline: Computational methods map ligand-target activity and noise in spatial transcriptomes
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell platforms now yield cell-resolved expression at scale, prompting benchmarks and methods for noise, localization and niche inference.

ranked.headline: Interactive platforms wrap omics analyses across spatial, proteomic and cancer datasets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications release Shiny apps, web servers and R packages that package established omics analyses behind accessible interfaces.

ranked.headline: Learned models read microtubule curvature and cell identity from fluorescence images
ranked.summary: Noisy and label-free imaging now yield quantitative readouts, with foundation models and synthetic data supporting segmentation benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Representation learning on bacterial proteomes and gene order for genomic inference
ranked.summary: Representation-learning models over protein and gene-content profiles are now applied to bacterial taxonomy, pathogenicity, and surveillance.

ranked.headline: Ion-level recovery, search engines, and spectrum benchmarks refine proteomics analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints target missing-value handling in DIA quantification and leakage-aware evaluation of MS/MS prediction tools.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools span DMS, scRNA-seq, assembly graphs, and GEO deposition
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 papers describe interactive, graphical tools that wrap existing QC, annotation, and visualization methods.

ranked.headline: Learning stochastic single-cell dynamics from snapshots, lineages and perturbations
ranked.summary: Snapshot, lineage and time-resolved single-cell data now support learning stochastic dynamics with interpretable model structure.

ranked.headline: Inferring selection, drift and shared ancestry from genome-wide polymorphism data
ranked.summary: Coalescent theory, admixture-graph drift decomposition and genome-wide scans now yield quantitative tests of selection and demography across species.

ranked.headline: New tools cover GWAS, variant pathogenicity, sequence alignment, and enrichment analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications describe GPU-accelerated, benchmarked, and learned-scoring implementations of core genomic analysis steps.

ranked.headline: DNA Language Model and Autoencoder Embeddings Applied to Unsupervised Genomic Assignment
ranked.summary: Recent papers pair DNA language model or autoencoder embeddings with unsupervised or graph learning for metagenomic and single-cell assignment.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of RNA processing and regulatory features across resolutions
ranked.summary: Single-cell and site-resolved RNA processing analyses now depend on benchmarked computational methods for polyadenylation and splicing inference.

ranked.headline: Personalized and reference-based models for high-dimensional biomedical data
ranked.summary: Recent work fits personalized, reference-based models to sparse or heterogeneous biomedical cohorts, with external validation emphasized.

ranked.headline: Haplotype and near-T2T assemblies expose structural variation in genome evolution
ranked.summary: Recent haplotype-resolved and near-T2T assemblies across fungi and plants expose structural variation and polyploid genome dynamics.

ranked.headline: Generative and structure-prediction models extend to noncanonical and cyclic peptides
ranked.summary: Pre-experimental models now target noncanonical residues, N-methylated cyclic peptides, and antimicrobial and nanobody design with explicit criteria.

ranked.headline: Parallel and memory-lean redesigns speed up core sequence alignment and search
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report GPU, SIMD and linear-space redesigns cutting memory and runtime in alignment and variant calling workflows.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking and workflow tools for long-read and RNA sequencing analysis
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and reproducible workflows address accuracy and reproducibility of long-read and RNA-seq analysis tools.

ranked.headline: Generative models are expanding and reshaping functional protein sequence space
ranked.summary: Generative AI and statistical energy models now design viable proteins and cells, including an E. coli strain built on a 19-amino acid alphabet.

ranked.headline: Oscillatory epigenomic dynamics, connectome chimera states and brain atlas geometry
ranked.summary: Current items tie oscillatory and linear dynamics, connectome structure and cross-species neuroanatomy to quantitative modeling.

ranked.headline: Methylation profiling methods benchmarked and refined across platforms and resolutions
ranked.summary: Cross-platform benchmarking and new segmentation and low-input methods now clarify how methylation and chromatin states are measured.
